name: rope
summary: rotary embedding, half-split pairing: x is T x H x Dh (Dh even), h = Dh/2; for i < h, x1 = x[t,j,i], x2 = x[t,j,i+h], c = cos[t,i], s = sin[t,i]: y[t,j,i] = x1 c - x2 s, y[t,j,i+h] = x1 s + x2 c
provenance: authored for OpenAccel Lab (Apache-2.0); the rotation is the GPT-NeoX/LLaMA half-split form. The cos and sin tables are inputs generated independently uniform in [-1,1]: the workload checks the rotation arithmetic only, table semantics (theta base 10000, positions 0..T-1) are out of scope because not every entrant has cos/sin.

y.why: each output is a length-2 dot product (x1 c - x2 s or x1 s + x2 c) of exact f32 inputs; with or without fused multiply-add and in either order it is within gamma(2) * (|x1 c| + |x2 s|) (Higham Thm 3.1/3.5), and reference.py passes that sum as the scale (WolframLanguageEvaluator: 2u/(1-2u), u=2^-24 -> 1.192e-7).
